subject: Sentinel Bio: partitioned hosting, limited audit window & pricing carveout
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentinelbio.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurements@sentinelbio.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Partitioned hosting + audit window — request and timing

Ethan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the great demo last week. We shared the draft SOW with our security and procurement teams; they came back with two items we need to address before we can sign:

1) Partitioned hosting: due to PHI handling, we need the private deployment to be logically partitioned inside our VPC so only our project namespace and storage are accessible to Sentinel engineers. Essentially a tenancy partition and strict egress rules.

2) Audit window: Security wants a timeboxed on-site audit window (48 hours) with physical access to logs and an engineer liaison. They will not accept open-ended audit access.

Both items are fine, but procurement is asking whether these constraints trigger a standard pricing concession — they informed me they expect at least a one-time implementation credit to cover engineering work and policy reviews. Can you confirm what level of commercial concession Redwood can offer?

Attached is the revised SOW with redlines (Sentinel_SOW_v2.pdf).

Best,
Elena
Head of Security Operations
Sentinel Bio

---
Attachment: Sentinel_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)

From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Partitioned hosting + audit window — request and timing

Folks, forwarding Sentinel's ask. Two asks combined: partitioned tenancy + a strict 48-hr audit window and physical log access liaison. Procurement is asking for a one-time engineering credit for us to make the configuration and update our procedures.

Quick context: Sentinel is a mid-market bio company, likely $150k ARR first year, multi-year potential. They want private deployment (VPC) with tighter isolation rules than our standard Private plan. They also insist on a timebound, on-site audit which is similar to previous asks but with stricter physical-access wording.

Action needed: 
- Legal: confirm whether the proposed audit language in their SOW is acceptable or needs fallback language (e.g., defined scope, redacted access, pre-scheduled visits).
- Infra/Engineering (Marcus): rough estimate of one-time work and an ETA for partitioned tenancy setup and the engineering validation we’d require.
- Sales (Marissa/Laura): commercial position on a one-time credit. I think we can consider a modest implementation credit (5–12%), but want exec signoff before committing.

I have attached the SOW from the customer. If this looks routine I will propose a fallback: 10% one-time credit + redacted/supervised audit with SIEM extracts instead of full physical access.

-Ethan
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Sentinel_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partitioned hosting + audit window — request and timing

Ethan — thanks for the ping. Quick read: legal will likely push back on unconstrained physical access; procurement will push for the credit.

Commercial recommendation: 10% one-time implementation credit (applied to first invoice) plus a capped professional-services day rate for any on-site engineering support beyond the 48-hour window. We should insist on:
- Audit must be scheduled with 30 days' notice and limited to the agreed scope in SOW appendix A.
- Physical access is escorted and limited to the liaison and logs; raw host-level access is not permitted.

If legal approves tightened wording, I can offer 10% now; anything above 10% needs VP sign-off.

Marissa
Enterprise Sales

---
On Wed, Dec 16, 2026 at 08:12 AM Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks, forwarding Sentinel's ask. Two asks combined: partitioned tenancy + a strict 48-hr audit window and physical log access liaison. Procurement is asking for a one-time engineering credit for us to make the configuration and update our procedures.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ethan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partitioned hosting + audit window — request and timing

Team,

Legal review summary (high level):
- Partitioned tenancy: acceptable if we document strict scoping and include a security responsibilities matrix. We will require that Sentinel does not request host-level root access and that all access is logged and reviewed.
- Audit window: we will not accept an open-ended audit clause. We can agree to a scheduled 48-hour window, escorted access, and delivery of a scoped set of artifacts (logs, SIEM exports, audit report).
- KMS / key material: we need clarity on whether they want Redwood to manage keys or bring-your-own (BYOK). BYOK will require an additional KMS integration and a runbook. That raises the implementation effort.

Commercial/legal ask: Given the non-standard operational work (partitioned tenancy + possible KMS integration + supervised audit), I recommend a one-time implementation credit of 12% OR a smaller credit (7%) plus a capped PS (professional services) commitment for any on-site work. We should also include the following clauses in the SOW appendix: 
  * Defined audit scope (Appendix A)
  * No host-level access; only API/agent and log extracts
  * KMS integration scope & timeline if BYOK chosen

I attach a proposed redline for the audit language (Redwood_Audit_Proposal.docx). If the VP signs off on a 12% concession we can accept BYOK with a 6-week delivery window; otherwise, we present the 7% + PS option.

-Kim
Head of Legal (Contracts)

---
Attachment: Redwood_Audit_Proposal.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 45KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partitioned hosting + audit window — request and timing

Team — I reviewed. Given the strategic angle (Sentinel is a strong reference in life sciences and they have high expansion potential), I approve the following commercial & contractual path:

Decision (exec approval):
- One-time implementation credit: 12% applied to first invoice (non-recoupable).
- BYOK/KMS: we will offer BYOK but require customer to cover KMS integration PS time; estimate 6 weeks SLA for the integration.
- Audit: approve a scheduled 48-hour escorted audit with pre-approved Appendix A artifact list; no host-level access.
- PS cap: if any on-site engineering is required beyond the 48 hours, it will be billed at standard hourly PS rates with a $10k cap unless pre-approved by VP/Sales.

Conditions:
1) Customer must sign the redlined SOW and Appendix A (audit scope) and accept the BYOK PS estimate if they choose BYOK.
2) DocuSign envelope must be returned within 14 days of this approval or the credit offer is void.

Marissa — please communicate the revised commercial terms to the customer and prepare the final SOW with Kim's redlines. Marcus — please prepare a short implementation estimate and a one-page runbook bulleting the KMS integration steps.

I'll loop CFO if Sentinel pushes for a larger discount.

-Laura
VP, Sales Operations
